title: Nintendo Reveals New Zelda LEGO Set Featuring Link and Epona for the Series’ 40th Anniversary
description: Nintendo has revealed a new The Legend of Zelda LEGO set featuring Link and Epona, alongside a playable Ocarina, during Zelda’s 40th Anniversary Direct.
body:
Nintendo has announced a new **The Legend of Zelda LEGO set featuring Link and Epona** during the franchise’s 40th Anniversary Direct.

The reveal expands a Zelda LEGO lineup that is still surprisingly young and gives the collaboration a very different kind of display piece: instead of centering another dungeon or boss encounter, this set puts Link beside one of his most recognizable companions.

Nintendo also showed a **playable Ocarina** among its anniversary products during the presentation.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: The newly announced LEGO The Legend of Zelda set featuring Link riding Epona, revealed during Nintendo’s Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct.
imageCredit: Nintendo / The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct

contentBlocks.text: The new Zelda LEGO set pairs **Link with Epona**, immediately giving it a different identity from the larger location-focused Zelda builds released so far. Nintendo revealed the set during its September 8 anniversary presentation as part of a wider collection of products celebrating 40 years of The Legend of Zelda.
contentBlocks.heading: What Nintendo announced

contentBlocks.text: The announcement comes only a short time after LEGO expanded the franchise with **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time – The Final Battle**, the 1,003-piece set released in March 2026. LEGO described that build as only the **second** full LEGO set based on The Legend of Zelda, following the Great Deku Tree 2-in-1. That makes Link and Epona another meaningful expansion of a collection that has moved from a single premium Zelda set into a broader line remarkably quickly.
contentBlocks.heading: Zelda’s official LEGO line is still very new

contentBlocks.text: The LEGO reveal was not Nintendo’s only physical-product announcement during the Direct. The presentation also showed a **playable Ocarina**, a particularly fitting anniversary item given the continued attention surrounding *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time*. The instrument is a separate product from the LEGO set, but both announcements draw heavily on some of the series’ most recognizable imagery.
contentBlocks.heading: Nintendo also showed a playable Ocarina

contentBlocks.text: Nintendo has confirmed the products themselves, but regional store information can appear at different times during a live reveal. Until Nintendo or LEGO publishes complete listings, pricing and release timing should be treated separately from the confirmed announcement. Neural Critic will update this story when those details are officially available.
contentBlocks.heading: Pricing and release details are the next things to watch

conclusion: For Zelda collectors, the interesting part is not simply that another LEGO set exists. Nintendo and LEGO are rapidly turning what began as a very limited collaboration into a recognizable Zelda product line, and Link with Epona gives it an immediately iconic centerpiece that is distinct from the Great Deku Tree and Final Battle sets.
